headline: Building AI Agents is notoriously difficult, despite viral demos and hype
summary: While demos show agents booking flights and writing code, their autonomous nature introduces complex engineering hurdles in planning, tool use, and error recovery.
details: AI agents have rapidly become a hot topic, with social media full of impressive demonstrations showing them booking flights, writing code, and automating complex workflows. These demos often make building an AI agent seem relatively simple, suggesting a basic connection between a large language model and a few APIs.

However, unlike traditional chatbots that operate within a single conversation, AI agents are designed to plan, make decisions, use external tools, adapt to changing situations, and recover from mistakes autonomously. This leap from generating text to taking reliable action introduces a new set of engineering challenges that many teams underestimate.

A primary difficulty lies in planning. Humans effortlessly break down large problems, but for machines, dynamically adjusting a plan when variables change is remarkably hard. Research from Arizona State University, titled 'LLMs Can't Plan,' highlights that while LLMs excel at pattern recognition, their innate ability to generate autonomous, executable plans in complex, changing environments is deeply flawed.

Tool interaction also presents significant fragility. For an agent to execute its plan, it must interact with the outside world via software APIs, databases, or web browsers. In production, agents encounter real-world infrastructure issues like invalid inputs, API timeouts, unexpected schema changes, and rate limits.

Unlike human developers who instinctively build error-handling into code, an AI agent must figure out how to handle these errors on the fly. If an API returns a raw HTML error page instead of the expected clean JSON, the agent often misinterprets the data, hallucinates, or crashes entirely. Managing memory for long-running tasks adds further complexity.

headline: Apple reportedly has three more unannounced iOS 27 features in the pipeline
summary: Despite a comprehensive WWDC 2026 keynote, a new report suggests Apple is holding back at least three significant iOS 27 features for a later reveal.
details: A report from 9to5Mac indicates that Apple has three unannounced features still in the pipeline for iOS 27. These functionalities were not revealed during the company's recent WWDC 2026 keynote.

Apple's WWDC 2026 keynote this week outlined many of its major new software features for the coming operating system. However, the report suggests that not all planned additions for iOS 27 have been publicly disclosed yet.
The specific details of these three features remain unknown at this time. Their existence implies that Apple may have further updates or announcements planned beyond the initial WWDC presentation.
This suggests that users might see additional iOS 27 capabilities introduced at a later date. The report does not specify when these features might be unveiled or what they entail.
